530:
(a) In order for the county solid waste management department to safely and cost effectively manage solid waste generated within the county, all restricted waste proposed for acceptance by the county solid waste management department is subject to a required decision process of materials/substance identification. In outline, the procedure for accepting restricted waste will include the following steps:
(1) All generators, established or new, must inform the county solid waste management department of the need to dispose of waste.
(2) The generator must specify in writing the source and materials contained in the waste.
(3) Analytical characterization of the county solid waste management department. Such analyses will be performed by an independent laboratory, at the expense of the generator.
(4) Additional costs incurred by the county solid waste management department in the disposal operation of restricted waste will be borne by the generator. These costs will be determined by the county solid waste management department.
(5) The county solid waste management department will make all determinations and decisions as to the acceptability of the waste.
(6) The acceptance and handling of all restricted waste will be documented in writing, and such documentation will be maintained for 30 years after closure of the county solid waste management facility. Documentation will include:
a. A waste profile form;
b. An analytical sampling plan and analytical results, as appropriate, including laboratory identification;
c. A signed county solid waste management department waste acceptance form having acceptance or rejection noted, with the reason indicated; and
d. A disposal contract.
(b) A list of all generators or restricted wastes that have had waste accepted or have otherwise demonstrated waste acceptability to the county solid waste management department will be maintained by the county solid waste management department. Any generator proposing to dispose of restricted waste must be listed before the county solid waste management department personnel will accept such waste.
(c) Policies and procedures for specific restricted waste such as asbestos, drums, liquids, dewatered latex waste, electrical distribution equipment and capacitors, petroleum-contaminated soils are available. Other materials and substances may be added to the specific restricted waste category, and it is the responsibility of the generator to remain apprised of such additions. All generators having contracts with the county solid waste management department will be notified of such actions.
(d) In all cases priority will be given to domestic waste, industrial waste and commercial waste generated in the county.
(1) Only domestic and commercial solid waste generated within the county is permitted to be disposed of at the county solid waste management facilities, and the tipping fee for this type of waste will be charged for such use.
(2) It is the intention of the county solid waste management department to accept only industrial wastes that have been approved by the environmental protection division and deemed appropriated by the county solid waste management department. All such wastes will be evaluated as to origin, chemical composition and quantity.
(3) No hazardous waste will be accepted. No person shall deposit or attempt to deposit hazardous waste on the county solid waste landfill property or other county property. No material other than commercial, municipal or industrial waste that has been approved by the environmental protection division and the county solid waste management department may be deposited at the landfill.
(4) Biomedical waste from sources generating less than 100 pounds per month may be deposited in the county landfill. All persons delivering biomedical waste shall declare the biomedical waste at the time it is delivered for disposal. Biomedical waste generating over 100 pounds per month may not be disposed of in the county landfill unless it is treated and deemed acceptable by the county solid waste management department.
(5) Asbestos must be wetted and bagged in 12-mil (minimum) thickness polyethylene bags or must be wetted, packed in six-mil polyethylene bags in fiber drums. Only asbestos waste generated in the county may be accepted. All state environmental protection division rules and regulations must be followed with respect to wetting and bagging the materials. Materials must be wet when received at the county solid waste management facilities. A surcharge per ton as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file in the office of the county clerk will be added for the special handling required by asbestos waste. The county solid waste management department must be given an advance notice of the intent to dispose of asbestos waste at its facilities, and asbestos waste will be accepted for disposal by appointment only.
(6) Bulky waste will be accepted if generated in the county, with the following exceptions.
a. Appliances with chlorofluorocarbon-containing refrigerant such as air conditioners, refrigerators, freezers, etc.
b. Carpet wastes from a manufacturer, including carpet scraps, ends and "strings" from the manufacturing process will be accepted if bailed or shredded at the fee rate noted in section 66-40. If carpet wastes are not bailed or shredded, a surcharge per ton as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file in the office of the county clerk will be added for extra volume and handling.
c. Cardboard carpet rolls unless baled or cut into four-foot lengths.
(7) Construction and demolition waste that originates in the county will be accepted if it does not contain any industrial waste components.
(8) Tires will be accepted only from the county.
(9) Prior to depositing their loads at the county solid waste management facilities, all haulers must declare loads that consist, in whole or in part, of outside of county solid waste; if a load that includes outside county solid waste is deposited at the county solid waste management facilities, 200 percent of the tipping fee for county solid waste shall be applied and charged to the entire load.
(Ord. of 5-18-93(2), § 9)

538:
The Catoosa County Board of Commissioners finds that litter found throughout Catoosa County often finds its way into the county's streams, rivers and lakes and detracts from the quality of life for the citizens of Catoosa County. Pollutants carried into the county's streams, rivers, and lakes by litter diminish the quality of the county's water and its aquatic resources. The Catoosa County Board of Commissioners deems it necessary to adopt this litter control ordinance in order to provide a prohibition against littering and to provide an enforcement mechanism with penalties for dealing with those found littering.
This article is modeled on the "Georgia Litter Control Law" (O.C.G.A. § 16-7-40 et. seq.) and the adoption of this article is authorized by the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 16-7-48.
(Ord. No. 06-007, § 1, 5-25-06)
539:
(1) Purpose and intent. The purpose of this article is to protect the public health, safety, environment, and general welfare of the citizens of Catoosa County, through the regulation and prevention of litter. The objectives of this article are to:
(a) Provide for uniform prohibition throughout the unincorporated areas of Catoosa County of any and all littering on public or private property; and
(b) Prevent the desecration of the beauty and quality of life of the citizens of Catoosa County and to prevent harm to the public health, safety, environment, and general welfare of said citizens, including the degradation of water and aquatic resources caused by litter.
(2) Applicability. This article shall apply to all public and private property located within the unincorporated areas of Catoosa County, Georgia.
(3) Compatibility with other regulations. This article is not intended to interfere with, abrogate, or annul any other ordinance, rule or regulation, statute, or other provision of law. The requirements of this article should be considered minimum requirements, and where any provision of this article impose restrictions different from those imposed by any other ordinance, rule or regulation, or other provision of law, whichever provisions are more restrictive or impose higher protective standards for human health or the environment shall be considered to take precedence.
(4) Severability. If the provisions of any article, section, subsection, paragraph, subdivision or clause of this article shall be judged invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction, such order of judgment shall not affect or invalidate the remainder of any article, section, subsection, paragraph, subdivision or clause of this article.
(Ord. No. 06-007, § 2, 5-25-06)

(1) Violations. It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision or fail to comply with any of the requirements of this article. Any person who has violated or continues to violate the provisions of this article may be subject to the enforcement actions outlined in this section or may be restrained by injunction or otherwise sentenced in a manner provided by law.

(a) Whenever litter is thrown, deposited, dropped or dumped from any motor vehicle, boat, airplane, or other conveyance in violation of this article, it shall be prima facie evidence that the operator of the conveyance has violated this article.
(b) Except as provided in subsection (a), whenever any litter which is dumped, deposited, thrown or left on public or private property in violation of this article is discovered to contain any article or articles, including, but not limited to, letters, bills, publications or other writing, which display the name of the person thereon in such a manner as to indicate that the article belongs or belonged to such person, it shall be a rebuttable presumption that such person has violated this article.
(3) Penalties. Any person who violates this article shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished as follows:
(a) By a fine of not less than $200.00 and not more than $1,000.00 per violation; and
(b) In addition to the fine set out in subsection (a) above, the violator shall reimburse Catoosa County for the reasonable cost of removing the litter when the litter is or is ordered removed by Catoosa County; and

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to own, establish, operate or maintain a hazardous waste facility in the unincorporated areas of the county unless such facility is in compliance with all of the conditions set forth in this article on hazardous waste facilities.

Administrative fee means a component of an occupation tax which approximates the reasonable cost of handling and processing the occupation tax.
Board means the board of commissioners of Catoosa County, Georgia, or the governing authority of Catoosa County, Georgia, if other than a board of commissioners.
Business includes, but is not necessarily limited to, an individual, practitioner, partnership, corporation or other entity engaged in an occupation, profession or other venture within the unincorporated areas of the county for the purpose of generating revenue.
County means the County of Catoosa, a political subdivision of the State of Georgia.
Employee shall have the definition and meaning described in the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 48-13-5(1.1), which said provisions are expressly incorporated by reference herein.
Location or office shall include any structure or vehicle where a business, profession, or occupation is conducted, but shall not include a temporary or construction work site which serves a single customer or project or a vehicle used for sales or delivery by a business or practitioner of a profession or occupation which has a location or office. The renter's or lessee's location which is the site of personal property which is rented or leased from another does not constitute a location or office for the personal property's owner, lessor, or the agent of the owner or lessor. 594:
(1) Businesses located within the county. Each and every business, practitioner, profession or occupation with a location or office lying solely within the unincorporated areas of the county shall be subject to and shall pay an occupation tax according to the number of full time or full time equivalent employees employed by the business, practitioner, profession or occupation. In order to establish the number of full time or full time equivalent employees, the county shall utilize the criteria set forth in O.C.G.A. § 48-13-10(a). The amount of the occupation tax imposed on each category of business, practitioner, profession or occupation shall be the amount described and shown on Table 1.1 which is attached hereto and made a part hereof.
(2) Businesses located outside the county. Pursuant to the authority granted by the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 48-13-7, each and every business, practitioner, profession or occupation which has no location or office within the boundaries of the county or the State of Georgia shall pay an occupation tax hereunder provided the business, practitioner, profession or occupation:
(a) Has one or more employees or agents who exert substantial efforts within the unincorporated areas of the county for the purpose of soliciting business or serving customers or clients; or
(b) Owns personal or real property which generates income and which is located in the unincorporated areas of the county.
The occupation tax imposed upon businesses, practitioners, professions or occupations pursuant to this section shall be based upon the number of employees and shall be in the amount described and shown on Table 1.1 which is attached hereto and made a part hereof.
(3) Purpose and scope of occupational tax. The occupation tax imposed hereunder shall be applicable only to those businesses, practitioners, professions and occupations described and authorized by the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 48-13-5 through O.C.G.A. § 48-13-26. The occupation tax is imposed by the county for revenue purposes and not for regulatory purposes. The payment of the occupation tax imposed hereunder shall not be deemed as a condition precedent to the payment of any particular trade, profession or occupation.
(4) Registration requirements.
(a) Each and every business, profession, practitioner or occupation subject to payment of the occupation tax hereunder shall be required to obtain an annual registration and/or license from the county evidencing payment of the required tax. The registration shall be issued by the county manager or such other office of the county as may be designated by the board from time to time.
(b) Prior to obtaining the required annual registration and paying the occupation tax, each business, profession, practitioner or occupation shall complete an application identifying the primary or dominant line of business being conducted and the number of employees employed by the business, profession, practitioner or occupation. If a business, profession, practitioner or occupation includes more than one line of business or is operated at more than one location or office, the number of employees employed at each location or office shall be entered on a separate application and the number of employees employed in each different line of business identified shall be disclosed and provided on the application.
(c) Only employees of a business, profession, practitioner or occupation who actually work within the boundaries of the county shall be counted for occupation tax purposes. Upon request by the county, a business, profession, practitioner or occupation with a location or office situated in more than one jurisdiction shall provide information concerning the names and numbers of employees who work within and outside the county.
(d) The required license/registration shall be displayed in a conspicuous place if the business, profession, practitioner or occupation has a permanent location or office within the county. If the business, profession, practitioner or occupation does not have a permanent location or office within the county, said registration shall be displayed to the county manager or any county codes enforcement officer upon request.
(5) Administrative fee. The occupation tax collected hereunder includes an administrative fee in order to offset the cost and expenses incurred by the county in administering this article and handling and processing the occupation tax collected hereunder.
(6) Collection and payment of occupation tax.
(a) The occupation tax due hereunder (including the necessary application for said tax) shall be paid each calendar year. The application shall be provided and occupation tax paid on an annual basis on January 1 of each year and shall be delinquent if not paid by March 1 of each year.
(b) Any new business, profession, practitioner or occupation commencing business in the county during a calendar year shall file the application and pay the full amount of the occupation tax within ten days of beginning to transact business within the county. Provided, however, if a business, profession, practitioner or occupation commences business in the county after July 1 of any given year, the amount of occupation tax due shall be 50 percent of the actual occupation tax amount for the calendar year in which business was commenced. However, any business, profession, practitioner or occupation commencing business after July 1 shall not receive a reduction in the administrative fee and any profession or practitioner electing to pay the occupation tax described in subsection (7) hereunder shall not receive a reduction in said tax if business is commenced after July 1 of any given calendar year.
(7) Occupation tax for certain professions. All practitioners of those professions enumerated in the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 48-13-9(c)(1)—(18) shall make an election to pay the required occupation tax using either of the following criteria:
(a) Based upon the number of full time and/or full time employees employed in the business, profession, practitioner or occupation as more particularly set forth on Table 1.1 which is attached hereto and made a part hereof; or
(b) Based upon a fee/tax imposed per practitioner licensed to perform or provide the service provided by the business or profession. Said fee/tax shall be paid at the practitioner's location or office and said per-practitioner fee/tax applies to each person in the business or profession who qualifies as a practitioner under applicable state regulatory guidelines and laws. A practitioner electing to pay the fee/tax under this subsection shall not be required to furnish the county with information or documents concerning the gross receipts of the business or profession. The fee/tax paid pursuant to this subsection is set forth on Table 1.2 which is attached hereto and made a part hereof.
The election required hereunder shall be made on an annual basis and must be made on or before January 1 of each calendar year. This subsection shall not apply to practitioners whose office is maintained by and who is employed in practice exclusively by the government of the United States, State of Georgia, or any county or any municipality of the State of Georgia. Said individuals shall not be required to pay the occupational tax or file any applications required hereunder.
(8) Multiple locations within the county. When a business, profession, practitioner or occupation conducts and/or transacts business at more than one fixed location or office within the unincorporated areas of the county, each location or office shall be considered a separate and distinct business, profession, practitioner or occupation for the purposes of payment of the occupation tax required hereunder.
(9) State registration and licensure.
(a) Any business, profession, practitioner or occupation which is required to be licensed by the Georgia Secretary of State pursuant to the provisions of Title 43 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated shall provide the county with evidence of the required state licensure prior to commencing business within the county and prior to paying the occupation tax required hereunder and being issued any registration by the county.
(b) Any business, profession, practitioner or occupation required to obtain health permits, bonds, certificates of qualification, certificates of competency or other regulatory permits, registrations qualifications or licenses shall provide the county with evidence that all qualifications are current and met prior to commencing business within the county and prior to paying the occupation tax required hereunder and being issued any registration by the county.
(c) Each business, profession, practitioner or occupation required to maintain any license, permit, bond, certificate or registration referenced in this section shall conspicuously post the same at the location or office of the business, profession, practitioner or occupation and it shall continue to be posted as long as the license, permit, bond, certificate or registration remains valid.
(Ord. No. 09-006, § IV, 7-7-09)

(1) Inspection of books and records. All businesses, professions, practitioners or occupations subject to the requirements of this article shall keep and maintain current business records concerning the operations of said business. The county manager, through his officers, agents, employees and representatives, may inspect the books or records of any business, profession, practitioner or occupation which is subject to the requirements of this article and said books or records shall be submitted for inspection within 30 days of the date a request for inspection is made. Any records, books or information provided to or reviewed by the county shall, pursuant to the requirements of O.C.G.A. § 48-13-15 and shall not be subject to disclosure under the provisions of the Georgia Open Records Act.
(2) Delinquent penalties. In the event any occupation tax, administrative fee or regulatory fee remains unpaid for a period of 90 days after its due date, a delinquent penalty equal to ten percent of the occupation tax, administrative fee or regulatory fee shall be due and payable. In addition, interest shall accrue on unpaid occupation taxes, administrative fees or regulatory fees at the rate of one and one-half percent per month until paid.
(3) Enforcement. In addition to all civil and criminal remedies authorized by this article, the Code of Catoosa County and Georgia Law, the officer charged with the collection of the occupation tax, administrative fee or regulatory fee hereunder shall be permitted to issue executions against any business, profession, practitioner or occupation for the amounts authorized by O.C.G.A. § 48-13-26. In addition, a civil fine may be imposed by a court of competent jurisdiction in an amount up to the maximum permitted by the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 48-13-26.
(4) Transaction of business. No business, profession, practitioner or occupation shall transact business or collect fees or monies from the transaction of business in the county unless and until all requirements of the ordinance are met and all occupation taxes, administrative fees and regulatory fees are paid current. Any business, profession, practitioner or occupation (which includes the person or persons soliciting for or representing said entities) which transacts business in the county in violation of this article or while any fees or taxes due hereunder are delinquent shall be subject to any and all remedies and penalties available under this article, the Code of Catoosa County or Georgia law.

1.04.01 Generally
A. This UDC shall apply only to the unincorporated areas of Catoosa County, Georgia, as now or hereafter established.
B. No building, structure, or land shall be used or occupied; no land shall be subdivided; and no building, structure, or part thereof shall be erected, constructed, reconstructed, moved, enlarged, or structurally altered unless in conformity with the provisions and requirements of this UDC.
C. A change of use shall conform to the provisions and requirements of this UDC.
D. Agricultural activities subject to Best Management Practices for Agricultural Businesses shall be regulated by the Georgia Department of Agriculture and USDA, and enforcement shall be the responsibility of said agencies.
1.04.02 Exemptions and Exceptions
The following general conditions or circumstances are exempt from the provisions and requirements of this UDC:
A. Buildings or structures that are legally under construction on the date of adoption of this UDC;
B. Buildings or structures for which a building permit has been issued as of the effective date of this UDC, provided that construction commences prior to the expiration of the building permit, and continues until completed;
C. Development pursuant to an approved development plan or subdivision plat approved prior to the effective date of this UDC, provided that development commences not later than one year after the effective date of this UDC; or
D. The proposed use of property lawfully approved as of the effective date of this UDC.

1.06.01 Generally
A. In the interpretation and application of the UDC all standards, provisions, and requirements shall be liberally construed in favor of the objectives and purposes of Catoosa County and shall not be construed to limit nor repeal any other powers granted under state or federal statutes.
B. Specific provisions of this UDC shall be followed in lieu of general provisions that may be in conflict with the specific provision.
C. The text of this UDC shall be followed in lieu of any caption, illustration, summary table, or illustrative table that may be in conflict with the text.
D. Where provisions of the UDC conflict with other regulations of the Catoosa County Code of Ordinances or construction codes identified in Section 1.09.00 of this UDC, the more stringent restrictions shall be applied.
E. The Article, Section and paragraph headings and enumerations used in this UDC are included solely for convenience and shall not affect the interpretation of the UDC.
1.06.02 Responsibility for Interpretations
A. In the event that any question arises concerning the application of regulations, standards, definitions, development criteria, or any other provision of this UDC, the Zoning Administrator shall be responsible for interpretation. In the interpretation of this UDC, the Zoning Administrator shall be guided by the Catoosa County Comprehensive Plan and applicable state or federal law. The Director may also refer any issue to the County Attorney, the Catoosa County Planning Commission (Planning Commission), or to the Catoosa County Board of Commissioners (Board of Commissioners) for their determination.
B. Responsibility for interpretation by the Zoning Administrator as set forth in this section shall be limited to standards, regulations, and requirements of the UDC, and shall not be construed to include interpretation of any technical codes adopted by reference in the UDC. Interpretation shall not be construed to override the responsibilities assigned by the Board of Commissioners, the Planning Commission, or to any commission, board, or official named in other sections or chapters of the UDC.
C. The Building Official shall be authorized to render interpretations of the State Minimum Standard Codes for Construction, which are consistent with their intent and purpose.
D. The Catoosa County Stormwater Director shall be authorized to render interpretations of Article III of this UDC which are consistent with its intent and purpose.
1.06.03 Zoning District Boundary Interpretations
Interpretations regarding boundaries of zoning districts described in Article II shall be made by the Zoning Administrator in accordance with the following:
A. Boundaries shown as approximately following the centerlines of streets or highways, street lines, or highway rights-of-way lines shall be construed as following such centerlines.
B. Boundaries shown as approximately following any platted lot, deed or tax parcel lines shall be construed as following such line.
C. Boundaries shown as approximately parallel to the centerlines of streets, highways or railroads, or rights-of-way of same shall be construed as being parallel to such centerlines and at such distance therefrom as indicated on the zoning map. If no distance is given, such dimension shall be determined by the use of the scale shown on said zoning map.
D. Where a district boundary line, as appearing on the zoning map divides a lot in single ownership at the time of enactment of this UDC, the district requirements for the least restricted portion of such lot shall be deemed to apply to the whole thereof, provided that such extensions shall not include any part of such a lot more than 200 feet beyond the district boundary line, so long as this use does not infringe on the buffer as otherwise provided in this UDC.
1.06.04 Permissible Land Use Interpretations
Interpretations regarding a requested use that is not identified as a permissible land use in Article II shall be made by the Zoning Administrator in accordance with Section 2.03.02 of this UDC.
1.06.05 Construction of Words and Phrases
A. Words used in the present tense include the future tense.
B. Words used in the singular number include the plural, and words used in the plural include the singular.
C. The word "person" includes a firm, association, organization, partnership, corporation, trust, limited liability company, and company as well as an individual.
D. The word "lot" includes the words "plot," "tract," or "parcel."
E. The word "building" is included in the word "structure."
F. The words "shall," "must," "will," "is to," and "are to" are always mandatory.
G. The conjunction "and" indicates that all the connected items, conditions, provisions, or events shall apply.
H. The conjunction "or" indicates that the connected items, conditions, provisions, or events may apply singly or in any combination.
I. The use of "either…or" indicates that the connected items, conditions, provisions, or events shall apply singly and not in combination.
J. The words "includes" or "including" shall not limit a term to the specific example but is intended to extent its meaning to all other instances or circumstances of like kind or character.
K. The word "day" means a calendar day.
L. The word "month" means a calendar month.
M. The word "week" means seven days.
N. The word "year" means a calendar year.
O. The word "used" or "occupied" as applied to any land or building shall be construed to include the words "intended, arranged or designed to be used or occupied."
P. The word "map," "zoning map," or "Catoosa County Zoning Map" means the "Official Zoning Map of Catoosa County, Georgia."
Q. References in this UDC to another section hereof, shall also include references to the subsections of such section.
R. References to a subsection shall include any portions of the section (including its other subsections) within which the subsection (being referred to) is located that are needed to construe such subsection (being referred to).
1.06.06 Computation of Time
A. Except as otherwise provided by time period computations specifically applying to other laws, when a period of time measured in days, weeks, months, years or other measurements of time except hours is prescribed for the exercise of any privilege or the discharge of any duty, the first day shall not be counted but the last day shall be counted; and, If the last day falls on Saturday or Sunday, the party having such privilege or duty shall have through the following Monday to exercise the privilege or to discharge the duty.
1) When the last day prescribed for such action falls on a public and legal holiday as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 1-4-1, the party having the privilege or duty shall have through the next business day to exercise the privilege or to discharge the duty.
2) When the period of time prescribed is less than seven days, intermediate Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays shall be excluded in the computation.
B. Whenever a number of days is specified in this UDC, or in any permit, condition of approval, or notice provided in compliance with this UDC, the number of days shall be construed as consecutive calendar days.
1.06.07 Severability
It is intended that the provisions of this UDC be severable; and should any portion be held invalid, such invalidity shall not affect any other portion of this UDC.
